  • Industry observers note that staunton, VA — Secure Solar Futures, a provider of on-site clean energy to schools, local governments, and businesses, will build a 313-kilowatt solar power system installed at Preston Park Elementary School in Roanoke, VA.
  • A total of 531 bi-facial solar panels manufactured by VSUN Solar in Houston, TX, will be installed on the rooftop of the school located at 3142 Preston Avenue, NW, and will offset 67% of the power used by the school annually.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roanoke City Schools to Add 313 kW Solar Power System.

Industry observers note that staunton, VA — Secure Solar Futures, a provider of on-site clean energy to schools, local governments, and businesses, will build a 313-kilowatt solar power system installed at Preston Park Elementary School in Roanoke, VA. Construction of the system is expected later this year at no capital cost to the Roanoke Schools through a 25-year Power Purchase Agreement with Secure Solar Futures. Pardee Renewable Energy LLC, a subsidiary of Pardee Resources Company, will provide the majority of the capital for the solar system.

A total of 531 bi-facial solar panels manufactured by VSUN Solar in Houston, TX, will be installed on the rooftop of the school located at 3142 Preston Avenue, NW, and will offset 67% of the power used by the school annually.

In its first year, the school’s solar system will produce 421 megawatt hours of clean energy, enough to power 44 average Virginia homes and provide environmental benefits by avoiding 371 metric tons of carbon pollution, which is equal to the emissions produced by 87 gasoline-powered passenger vehicles, or the carbon sequestered by 372 acres of U.S. forests, according to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

In a recent development, under the Power Purchase Agreement, the solar power equipment will be provided at no upfront cost to Roanoke Schools. For the 25-year term of the agreement, Pardee Renewable Energy LLC, together with its partner Secure Solar Futures, will own, operate, and maintain the solar power system and will sell the energy produced to the school division at a rate lower than the local electric utility.

It has been revealed that during the term of the Power Purchase Agreement, Preston Park Elementary School will save $581,000 in net avoided costs for electricity. After the conclusion of the term, Roanoke Schools can opt to take ownership of the solar power system at a nominal cost, producing its own energy for the remainder of the equipment’s 35- to 40-year productive lifespan.

About Roanoke City Public Schools.

Recent findings suggest that roanoke City Public Schools (RCPS) is an urban school division in Roanoke, Virginia, serving a pre-K through 12th grade population of approximately 14,000 students. RCPS provides an inclusive and equitable, student-centered culture that empowers lifelong learning. Through meaningful, relevant, and engaging learning opportunities, we will empower all students to dream, excel, and meet their full potential to benefit our city and its citizens. The division has 17 elementary schools, five middle schools, two high schools, and five program locations, including the Roanoke Valley Governor’s School for Science & Technology and two career and technical education centers. Visit www.rcps.info for additional information.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dongfeng Nissan officially opened the early order book on its fresh NX7 hybrid yesterday, promising up to 320 km (~198 miles) of all-electric range from a 40 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery and a $20,000 price tag.

Sources indicate that when the first generation Nissan LEAF bowed with 70-ish miles of range from its 24 kWh li-ion battery pack, it struggled to meet widespread adoption, especially in an SUV-obsessed US market that demands forethought-free trips to Home Depot and bladder-busting range. The manufacturer’s latest 2027 Rogue Hybrid is a step in the right direction, using a gas engine to generate electricity for a pair of electric drive motors that deliver a driving experience that’s remarkably similar to a “pure” electric car – but without a plug, it’s still entirely dependent on fossil fuels. The new Dongfeng Nissan NX7, though? That’s a different story.

The plug-in hybrid Dongfeng Nissan NX7 might be called a “long range hybrid” in the same sense that Volvo’s Euro-market XC70 is, in that it’s an EV for the 360-odd days a year that you’re driving less than 200 miles, and an ICE vehicle for the handful of days you drive more. And if you’re one of those people who thinks stopping on road trips is a character flaw, a fully charged and topped off NX7 will take you an astonishing 1,666 km (~1,035 miles) from where you started.

The fresh NX7 could be an ideal lilypad vehicle for North American drivers who are either too afraid of being caught without a charger or too invested in the outcome of one or more dumb oil wars to confidently make the switch to EV – and, even at twice the 129,900 yuan ($~19,400) asking price, I think it would be a hit.

For that money, NX7 buyers get an absolutely loaded Model Y-sized crossover (they’re within 1/4″ of each other in length), with a 17.3″ central touchscreen, a fully digital instrument cluster, and (on higher-spec models) a positively massive 55″ augmented-reality head-up display powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8295P automotive processor and running on Nissan OS 3.0 with an AI-powered voice assistant developed with iFlytek that, Nissan claims, can recognize natural-language commands, remember user preferences, and even recognize occupants, adjusting vehicle settings accordingly.

On top-shelf models, the NX7 cabins get “AI Zero-Pressure Cloud Blanket” seats that use sensors and air-cushion arrays to dynamically adjust for maximum comfort, and include heating, ventilation, and a 12-point SPA-level massage function. The front seats can be fully reclined to create a bed-like configuration that will be familiar to Cube owners. The NX7 even offers an on-board refrigerator and motion-sickness prevention system that Nissan claims can reduce motion sickness by as much as 83% (which, like, I wouldn’t want to be the one to test that – but seems cool).

Sources indicate that power comes from a 1.5-liter naturally aspirated internal combustion engine making 98 hp that’s paired to a 228 hp electric drive motor and the previously mentioned 40.9 kWh LFP battery. It’s not immediately clear if the NX7 uses a conventional parallel hybrid system like a Prius or a series-hybrid-plus-plug setup, but Dongfeng’s hybrid technology patents describe a pretty versatile arrangement with four possible operating modes: series hybrid, parallel hybrid, direct engine drive and electricity generation – which means the vehicle can theoretically use the ICE motor as a generator, drive the wheels mechanically, or work alongside the electric motor, depending on what the operating conditions call for. Whether any or all four modes make it to production on the NX7 remains to be seen, but it’s an intriguing bit of engineering for a vehicle promising nearly 200 miles of electric driving range.

#30. Breaking: A Record Number Of Uber Miles Are Happening In EVs

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (704 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Insideevs

Breaking: A Record Number Of Uber Miles Are Happening In EVs

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (704 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Uber’s electrification efforts are looking better with every quarter, and this year’s third quarter has shown that the giant ride-hailing tech giant is serious about lowering its fleet’s emissions.
  • Sources indicate that let’s focus on the good news first.
  • In Europe, one in five Uber trips were done in an EV, while one in ten Americans and Canadians who took an Uber in Q3 wound up in an electric car.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Uber’s electrification efforts are looking better with every quarter, and this year’s third quarter has shown that the giant ride-hailing tech giant is serious about lowering its fleet’s emissions. That said, Uber is also aware that, based on current trends, its 2030 goals “continue to be out of reach.”.

Sources indicate that let’s focus on the good news first. Last quarter, Uber drivers across the globe completed a whopping 207.4 million rides in EVs, which boils down to over 26 EV trips on the ride-hailing platform every second, on average. Compared to the same period last year, the number of EV trips on the platform is 52% higher, but the substantial stats don’t end here.

In Europe, one in five Uber trips were done in an EV, while one in ten Americans and Canadians who took an Uber in Q3 wound up in an electric car. On average, there were 434,000 EV drivers active on Uber from July through September globally, up 52% from the same period last year,.

When looking at the charts provided by the ride-hailing company, the difference between Europe and the U.S. and Canada is astonishing. Even from the start of the chart, in Q1 2021, Europe had a consistent lead when it comes to electrification, but the two North American countries were left in the dust starting in the third quarter of 2024. European drivers flocked to EVs, helped by various incentives and a boost in the charging infrastructure, while Americans' and Canadians’ uptake stayed relatively flat. For its part, Uber has offered cash bonuses to drivers who wanted to switch to an EV.

It has been revealed that despite the upward trends seen in the charts provided by Uber, it’s not all good news. The tech giant has missed almost all of its sustainability targets for 2025 and is well on its way to missing its goals for the end of 2030 by a wide margin.

Sources indicate that just as the number of EVs on the ride-hailing platform has increased, plenty of drivers chose gas- or diesel-powered cars to make an extra buck on Uber. In the U.S. and Canada, every mile that a passenger traveled on Uber resulted in an average generation of 318 grams of carbon dioxide. That’s better than 2024’s 340 grams, but worse than the 306-gram average in 2023.

Sources indicate that A similar story can be found in Europe, though the average vehicle emissions caused by Uber trips are vastly smaller than in the U.S. and Canada. Last year, 186 g of CO2 were put into the atmosphere in Europe for every mile traveled by a passenger on Uber. The figure is lower than in 2024 and 2023, but higher than the 183 g average in 2022.

According to recent reports, the manufacturer noted that the large gap between Europe and the U.S. and Canada can be linked to two factors. First, European drivers prefer EVs and hybrids more than American and Canadian drivers, but the more stringent fuel economy reporting standards in the U.S. also contribute to this discrepancy.

In 2025, the ride-hailing giant had wanted to see 100% of rides in London and Amsterdam be zero-emission. The outcome was just 41%. Furthermore, 50% of all mobility miles in seven European capitals were envisioned as being completed in electric vehicles, but the year ended with just 32%.

By the end of the decade, 100% of rides in Canada, Europe, and the U.S. should be zero-emission, but Uber is realistic and knows that it’s highly unlikely that it will finish 2030 with these numbers. Still, the company claims it’s “deeply committed to this transition,” even though many levers are outside of its control.

Breaking: This Fast Prototype Army Off-Roader Owes Its Existence To The Paris-Dakar Rally

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • While Donald Trump's been busy threatening our country's European allies and cozying up to Vladimir Putin instead, those allies have been making some military moves of their own.
  • The two countries each have separate 10% ownership stakes in John Cockerill Defense, which touts the i-X as the world's first "ground interceptor." In fact, that is what the "i" in the vehicle's name stands for.
  • The i-X also has to provide a military-grade driving experience to fill its role, and the Cockerill crew seems to have taken a slightly different approach from, say, GM.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While Donald Trump's been busy threatening our country's European allies and cozying up to Vladimir Putin instead, those allies have been making some military moves of their own. France and Belgium, for example, have been teaming up with John Cockerill Defense to support an innovative fresh approach to land vehicles — including the Cockerill i-X.

The two countries each have separate 10% ownership stakes in John Cockerill Defense, which touts the i-X as the world's first "ground interceptor." In fact, that is what the "i" in the vehicle's name stands for. The "X," in turn, refers to the vehicle's modular multi-weapons system. Plus, along with the ability to use machine guns and assorted rockets/missiles, the i-X features advanced technology such as onboard AI, various cameras/sensors, "Smart Helmet" integration, acoustic gunshot detection/location, and more.

The i-X also has to provide a military-grade driving experience to fill its role, and the Cockerill crew seems to have taken a slightly different approach from, say, GM. The General's infantry squad vehicle cost nearly $1 billion in taxpayer money, yet, at its core, it uses the same platform underpinning the Chevrolet Colorado production truck. Meanwhile, multiple sources — but not Cockerill itself – say the i-X is built on the foundation of a Paris-Dakar rally vehicle. The actual company behind that rally vehicle remains a mystery, but here's an interesting coincidence that hasn't been mentioned much by the media: France owns 15.01% of Renault, which owns Dacia, which supports the Dacia Sandrider — a purpose-built racer that won the 2026 Paris-Dakar rally. Whether that connection is anything more than a coincidence is anyone's guess, but it is fascinating.

According to recent reports, now, to be clear, the Cockerill i-X is still in testing, so its capabilities could change some before it goes into military production. That mentioned, the firm has released some preliminary specs based on the i-X prototypes. Cockerill is a bit vague on powertrains, but it looks like the company is currently touting two packages. One is based on a 750-horsepower V8,and the second is an 800-hp serial hybrid setup with an all-electric mode for about 18.6 miles of EV-style travel. Further incorporating a high-performance suspension, the i-X has a top speed of about 124 mph on the road and nearly 100 mph off-road.

Industry observers note that for some context, the Paris-Dakar Sandriders top out at 106 mph, which is the limit for their class — and the maximum allowed speed for any modern Paris-Dakar entry. GM's ISV we mentioned above? Yes, it has a different use case, and that's a good thing. The ISV isn't going to do too much ground intercepting with a top speed of 60 mph. After all, a fast tank, like the Rheinmetall KF51 Panther, can get up to 65 mph on the road. All of those numbers mean you can accurately describe the i-X as fast, at least for a military vehicle.

Sources indicate that the i-X is probably pretty fast off-road compared to production vehicles, too. True, automakers don't often let this kind of data out, but one source states first-gen Ford Raptor prototypes were able to exceed 100 mph off-road during testing. Of course, the Cockerill can't keep up with production vehicles on the road, where even the Hellcat-powered 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee full-size pickup is expected to hit 170 mph.

The Paris-Dakar rally — now known simply as Dakar – puts vehicles through some of the most extreme conditions on the planet, making the event a fantastic proving ground for military vehicles. And it's not only a test of peak performance. Covering thousands of miles, over all types of surfaces and through all sorts of weather, the rally also can be a showcase for extreme vehicular stamina. Consider: In the race's very first running, in 1978, only 74 of the 170 vehicles in the event were able to finish it. The numbers had improved to 247 finishers out of 317 entries in 2026, but that's still a lot of DNFs.

According to recent reports, as for the rally's name change, that's related to its route changes — it hasn't gone from Paris to Dakar, Senegal, since 2001. Ironically enough, given its connection to the Cockerill i-X, the race itself has had to travel around the world to avoid military conflicts. Much like F1's decision to cancel races earlier this year due to the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, the folks behind the Paris-Dakar rally have had to adjust their calendar based on who was fighting. Sometimes, this meant changing the route or the stopping and starting points, but organizers had to cancel the event entirely in 2008.

The situation got bad enough that the whole circus relocated to South America from 2009 to 2019, then moved to the Middle East — Saudi Arabia, to be exact — for the years since. The photo above demonstrates a Dacia Sandrider flying through the Saudi desert in 2026. The rally will take a one-year hiatus from that country next, running in Portugal and Morocco for 2027, before returning to Saudi Arabia in 2028.

Breaking: Rocket Fuel: The Last Frontier For Natural Gas

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1579 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fossil fuels are slowly beginning to lose their grip on the global transportation sector, with one key omission: rocket fuel.
  • Sources indicate that not all rocket fuel is methane-based, but that’s where some aerospace firms, including SpaceX, have landed in the pursuit of space domination.
  • With its future volume of launch operations in mind, SpaceX aims to exercise as much control as possible over its fuel supply.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fossil fuels are slowly beginning to lose their grip on the global transportation sector, with one key omission: rocket fuel. The rocket fuel conundrum has earned an uptick in attention in recent years, now that rocket launches, once rare, are becoming as commonplace as rush hour traffic. The Elon Musk venture SpaceX, for example, is building upcoming natural gas pipelines in order to produce its own methane-based propellant, needed to sustain the launch of many thousands of rockets in the coming years.

Sources indicate that not all rocket fuel is methane-based, but that’s where some aerospace firms, including SpaceX, have landed in the pursuit of space domination. Methane is processed from natural gas, stripping away nitrogen and other impurities. Liquefied and mixed with liquid oxygen, it becomes a powerful propellant.

With its future volume of launch operations in mind, SpaceX aims to exercise as much control as possible over its fuel supply. The company is investing in its own natural gas pipelines and on-site fuel production facilities to help ensure that the taps don’t run dry, though it still relies on the gas industry to find the stuff and bring it up from the ground.

Recent findings suggest that spaceX has already been sucking up a copious amount of natural gas for its existing operations in Texas and Florida. “SpaceX (SPCX) is emerging as one of the largest new customers for natural gas,” reported the oil and gas analytics firm East Daley in October.

In a recent development, “Unlike Falcon 9, which burns rocket-grade kerosene and liquid oxygen, Starship creates a direct link between launch activity and natural gas consumption. SPCX plans to process and liquefy pipeline gas into liquid methane to fuel the rockets,” East Daley elaborates.

As described by East Daley, the SpaceX subsidiary Coastal Connect Services is planning a 32.4-mile natural gas pipeline to hook up SpaceX operations in Cape Canaveral, Florida with existing infrastructure jointly owned by Kinder Morgan and Energy Transfer.

In a recent development, meanwhile, at the manufacturer’s launch site and newly incorporated (as of 2025) City of Starbase in Cameron County, Texas, looks are in motion for SpaceX affiliate Lone Star Mineral Development to connect the fresh 8-mile “Starpipe” natural gas pipeline with another 145-mile pipeline right now being built by the firms WhiteWater, Enbridge, and MPLX. Starpipe is expected to begin shuttling natural gas into Starbase Texas early next year.

In a recent development, the two pipeline projects come alongside word that SpaceX has nailed down approvals for parts of a new $100 billion project that expands the company’s US footprint into another combination city-and-launch-site under the name of Starbase, Louisiana. The new city will presumably also require a reliable supply of natural gas for on-site rocket fuel production.

It has been revealed that for the record, Starbase, Louisiana is not part of the educational non-profit organization STARBASE Louisiana, an affiliate of the national STARBASE program of the US Department of Defense, aimed at stimulating interest in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics) topics among 5th grade students. The Louisiana branch of STARBASE is located Barksdale Air Force Base in Bossier Parish, in the northwestern part of the state.

Starbase, Louisiana will take up 125,000 acres of land at Pecan Island in a marshy region along the southern coast in Vermilion Parish, where looks are being laid for 30 introduces per day. More than a dozen launch towers will eventually sprout up at the site, where the operation will include producing rocket fuel.

Recent findings suggest that if you’ve gotten wind of the project under the name “Osprey,” you’re not dreaming. The new city was reportedly code-named “Project Osprey” during initial discussions with public officials. As described by the Gulf State News affiliate WWNO (New Orleans Public Radio) on November 11, Project Osprey was shrouded in secrecy during the initial negotionas, with “dozens” of local officials signing non-disclosure agreements that limited what they could say about the project.

The Osprey code name also reportedly enabled Vermilion Parish officials to sidestep public participation in ostensibly public hearings on the Starbase, Louisiana project earlier this year. Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry finally let the cat out of the bag in a public announcement in August. Local residents and the nonprofit organization Vermillion Citizens coalition have already filed a lawsuit against the project, alleging that parish officials approved parts of Starbase, Louisiana in violation of the state’s Open Public Meetings Law.

If and when shovels hit the ground on Starbase, Louisiana, the Trump administration is taking steps to help ensure that natural gas producers in the US come through with the goods — not just for SpaceX, of course, although the firm has become a market-mover in the gas industry as noted by East Daley.

Industry observers note that on November 10, for example, the US Department of Energy declared the finishing touches on a $480 million loan in support of Project Elkhorn, an endeavor under the umbrella of the oil and gas firm Arena Energy. Project Elkhorn covers the modernization of 22 existing platforms off the Louisiana coast — coincidentally or not, the same state that expects to host the new Starbase city.

Arena launched in 1999 with a focus on revitalizing mature oil and gas fields. According to the Energy Department, Project Elkhorn will ramp natural gas production up to 77 million cubic feet per day at peak production among the 22 platforms, alongside up to 38,600 barrels of oil per day. By way of contrast, the 22 platforms right now produce 30,000 barrels of oil per day. Over the lifespan of Project Elkhorn, the collective total is expected to add 25 million barrels of oil and 250 billion cubic feet of natural gas to the US fossil energy roster.

It has been revealed that as CEO of the leading EV maker Tesla, Elon Musk has earned his share of credit for rescuing electric cars from the dustbin of automotive obscurity and vaulting them into the mainstream mobility market of today — if not so much here in the US, then certainly overseas. Musk’s other ventures, on the other hand, threaten to offset, if not override, whatever sustainability gains are to be made from EVs.

It has been revealed that in addition to SpaceX, Musk’s xAI data centers have also contributed to spiking demand for natural gas. Last year word dropped that Musk’s Colossus data center in Memphis, Tennessee trucked in approximately three dozen industrial-sized gas generators to power the site, at least 15 of which were already in operation without an air quality permit. The Southern Environmental Law Center has been among those raising the alarm over toxic emissions from the generators, which lack the pollution controls required of permanent power plants.

Natural gas also factors into a new data center planned for the SpaceX-backed City of Starbase, Texas, which sits adjacent to Brownsville. The city of Brownsville recently imposed a temporary moratorium on new data center construction. According to ABC News affiliate KVUE and other sources, earlier this year Elon Musk asked Brownsville officials to de-annex a parcel of land at its outskirts, evidently in order to building a $24 billion data center at the site along with a new gas-fired power plant for a new data center to be located in Starbase. The request was granted, enabling the project to skirt around the Brownsville moratorium.

Starbase city officials are scheduled to conduct a public hearing on the latest data center on December 9, where presumably they will decide whether or not the project can make due with gas generators until a full gas power plant with appropriate pollution controls can materialize.

Over and above the rocket fuel matter, grassroots activists, environmental organizations, and researchers have been raising the alarm over the impact of Starbase in Texas for years, tracking significant harm to local public recreation resources as well as wildlife habitats. Similar concerns have surfaced around SpaceX’s looks for Starbase, Louisiana.

Industry observers note that of course, nobody seriously expects the whole domestic rocket business to stop in its tracks. The matter is one of mitigating climate and biodiversity risks, developing projects that avoid pummeling vulnerable communities with additional public health risks, and investing in more sustainable options including alternative rocket fuels.

Keep an eye on the aviation industry for some hints at the future of sustainable propellants. Airline stakeholders have been focusing on SAF, generally meaning a bio-based equivalent of kerosene jet fuel. However, the going has been slow, and it’s even slower in the field of propellants. The European Space Agency, for example, has been exploring green propellants for space operations for 25 years, with little to show for its efforts.

According to recent reports, more recently, though, aviation stakeholders have begun turning to the emerging electrofuels or “solar fuels” industry, meaning fuels synthesized from captured carbon and green hydrogen, with solar and other renewables powering the operation. The green hydrogen industry has been struggling for traction, but signs of scaleup have finally emerged, with e-kerosene jet fuel in play along with green hydrogen. Honda, for one, is envisioning a fleet of reusable rockets propelled by renewable fuels, and at least two Chinese firms are also working the reusable rocket angle.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Getting an all-wheel-drive Tesla Model Y just got a lot more expensive after the American company removed the entry-level version of the crossover from its online configurator.

The Model Y All-Wheel Drive, which used to cost roughly $42,000, is nowhere to be found on the automaker’s website, which means the most affordable dual-motor Model Y is now the Premium AWD trim that starts at $51,630.

Industry observers note that introduced in February, the now-defunct Model Y AWD came hot on the heels of the budget-oriented Model 3 Standard and Model Y Standard that debuted in October 2025 as more affordable, rear-wheel-drive-only versions of the manufacturer’s best-selling EVs. When the bare-bones Model Y AWD was introduced, Tesla also dropped the “Standard” badge from its lineup, though the other trims are still called “Premium” and “Performance”.

Powered by the same battery as the single-motor Model Y RWD, the discontinued Model Y AWD had the shortest claimed range in the Model Y lineup, with an EPA-estimated 294 miles on a full charge—54 miles less than the most affordable rear-driven crossover in Tesla’s lineup at the moment.

With two electric motors providing motivation, the dropped Model Y AWD could sprint from zero to 60 miles per hour in 4.6 seconds, 2.2 seconds faster than its single-motor counterpart, despite weighing roughly 200 pounds more.

The cheapest Model Y in Tesla’s lineup remains the basic RWD version, which starts at $41,630. Compared to the better-equipped and more expensive trims, the entry-level crossover comes with redesigned front and rear lights, passive shock absorbers, a lower 225-kilowatt maximum charging power, fewer speakers for the audio system, and seats trimmed in vegan leather and cloth. There’s no FM radio, no rear screen, no ventilated seats, and only the front seats are heated. Furthermore, while the glass roof is still installed, the base trim has a headliner that covers it entirely.

Recent findings suggest that the discontinuation of the Tesla Model Y All-Wheel Drive is just the latest casualty in the firm’s quest to slim down its passenger-vehicle lineup. Earlier this year, the Model S and Model X were axed, and their production line has been ripped out of the factory to make room for robots. More recently, Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced that the Cybertruck would be retired next year. Until that happens, the only trim remaining is the top Cyberbeast, which starts at $109,990.

There are no plans to replace the Model S and Model X, and the Cybercab two-seater will take over the Cybertruck’s floor space.

#23. Latest Update: China’s electric airliner era starts with a 19-seat plane and 400 km of range

Latest Update: China’s electric airliner era starts with a 19-seat plane and 400 km of range

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (892 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • COMAC’s CE-25A, China’s 19-seat battery-electric commuter plane, flew with a crew for the first time on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong.
  • The CE-25A had already completed 19 autonomous test flights with nobody on board since February 2, and China’s aviation regulator is now reviewing it for a type certificate.
  • It has been revealed that the CE-25A is a T-tail commuter plane with 10 electric ducted fans on the wings, five per side, instead of propellers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

COMAC’s CE-25A, China’s 19-seat battery-electric commuter plane, flew with a crew for the first time on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong. Two pilots and a flight test engineer were aboard the roughly 10-tonne demonstrator, and COMAC says every system worked normally.

It wasn’t the plane’s first flight. The CE-25A had already completed 19 autonomous test flights with nobody on board since February 2, and China’s aviation regulator is now reviewing it for a type certificate.

It has been revealed that the CE-25A is a T-tail commuter plane with 10 electric ducted fans on the wings, five per side, instead of propellers. COMAC lists a 300 km/h cruise speed and a 400 km (250-mile) range.

Sources indicate that the CAAC accepting COMAC’s type certificate application starts the airworthiness review. It doesn’t mean paying passengers are close, and COMAC hasn’t given a date for commercial service.

It has been revealed that the program has been quiet for a long time. COMAC showed a CE-25A model at the China International Import Expo in Shanghai in November 2023, with a placard listing 400 to 500 km of range and a 400 km/h top cruise speed. The full-size aircraft, registered B-0EFH, only became public when photos leaked on Chinese social media on October 28.

Sources indicate that the obvious battery candidate is CATL. In July 2023, COMAC, CATL, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University formed a joint venture with CNY 600 million in registered capital to develop electric aircraft, as we reported when CATL launched its aviation unit.

It has been revealed that CATL had just unveiled its “condensed” battery at the time, claiming up to 500 Wh/kg at the cell level, and noted it was testing the cells to aviation standards. Neither manufacturer has confirmed what’s inside the CE-25A, though.

~500 Wh/kg has long been seen as the target for battery energy density to enable electric flight on a commercial scale.

COMAC isn’t alone in flying a large electric demonstrator. In August, Heart Aerospace flew its X1 in Plattsburgh, New York, for 27 minutes. It’s a 25,000-lb aircraft with a 106-foot wingspan, which Heart calls the largest battery-electric aircraft ever flown.

Eviation flew its 9-passenger Alice back in September 2022, then laid off most of its staff in early 2025.

Heart is the closest Western comparison. It dropped its 19-seat ES-19 for the 30-seat ES-30 back in 2022, and the ES-30 now relies on reserve turbogenerators to stretch its range, with BAE Systems working on the battery. Heart is targeting 2031 for service and claims “more than 40%” lower operating costs.

For years, the go-to excuse in the West for doing nothing about emissions was China. Why should we bother, the argument went, if China won’t? Now China is pulling ahead, and it’s doing it by cutting its dependence on fossil fuels.

According to recent reports, look at trucking. Electric trucks hit 50.3% of China’s heavy truck sales in September, and they’re already eating into the country’s diesel demand. In the US, electric models were about 0.3% of heavy-truck sales last year, according to the ICCT.

A great step in the right direction, probably needs a doubling in range but at current rates of progress that will only be five years away.

Now it’s planes, starting where batteries make sense today: short regional routes. The CE-25A’s 400 km shrinks once you keep the reserves regulators require, and a Beechcraft 1900 turboprop in the same class covers well over 1,000 km. So it’s not replacing turboprops anytime soon. But that’s how trucking started too. Short-haul first, then long-haul tractors once the batteries caught up.

According to recent reports, and this couldn’t happen fast enough. We’re in the middle of a diesel and jet fuel crisis. Jet fuel averaged $3.50 a gallon in early August, up 63% from a year earlier, according to Heart Aerospace. Every truck and plane China moves to batteries is one less exposed to that.

In a recent development, china also has the batteries to pull it off, with CATL in the joint venture. Meanwhile, Heart has pushed to 2031 and added a fuel-burning backup, and Eviation is a cautionary tale.

According to recent reports, if you’re following the electrification of transport, the cheapest place to start is your own roof: home solar can power your EV for close to nothing. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. Sonnen, SOLRITE, & ADAPT Energy, Integrating VPP Breakers to Turn Home Loads into Flexible Grid Assets

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • SOLRITE Unveils Next-Gen Virtual Power Plant Node with sonnen and ADAPT Energy, Integrating VPP Breakers to Turn Home Loads into Flexible Grid Assets.
  • ADAPT Energy’s control of VPP breakers will add dispatchable load flexibility to the SOLRITE sonnen VPP, while paving a simpler, faster, and lower-cost path to whole-home backup.
  • SOLRITE, a manufacturer specializing in developing, financing, and owning Virtual Power Plant Agreement (VPA) projects, together with Sonnen, a leader in Virtual Power Plant energy storage technology, revealed they will now digitally integrate VPP smart breakers, managed by ADAPT Energy, into the SOLRITE  sonnen VPP.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SOLRITE Unveils Next-Gen Virtual Power Plant Node with sonnen and ADAPT Energy, Integrating VPP Breakers to Turn Home Loads into Flexible Grid Assets.

ADAPT Energy’s control of VPP breakers will add dispatchable load flexibility to the SOLRITE sonnen VPP, while paving a simpler, faster, and lower-cost path to whole-home backup.

SOLRITE, a manufacturer specializing in developing, financing, and owning Virtual Power Plant Agreement (VPA) projects, together with Sonnen, a leader in Virtual Power Plant energy storage technology, revealed they will now digitally integrate VPP smart breakers, managed by ADAPT Energy, into the SOLRITE  sonnen VPP. The integration marks the next evolution of sonnen and SOLRITE’s industry-leading partnership in VPP innovation, expanding beyond battery storage by transforming residential electrical loads into flexible, dispatchable grid assets for both the VPP and smart backup power applications.

Unlike traditional approaches to whole-home backup, often requiring hard-wired circuit relocation, including exclusive loads panels, the newly expanded VPP Node combines the sonnenHub with ADAPT Energy’s VPP smart breaker technology to intelligently manage major household loads. This creates a more streamlined approach to whole-home backup while unlocking an entirely upcoming source of flexibility for the SOLRITE sonnen VPP. With homeowner permission, the VPP smart breaker—controlled by ADAPT Energy—can also participate in on-grid VPP events, enabling the same electrical infrastructure to be flexible for both backup and grid participation.

“Our work with ADAPT Energy is a meaningful step forward in how we think about residential battery storage and VPP participation,” mentioned Regan George, CEO and Founder of SOLRITE Energy. “We have already demonstrated the tremendous value of connecting sonnen batteries together as a pooled grid asset. Now, we’re going inside the home and unlocking another layer of flexibility that has been sitting there all along. By combining the battery with additional load management made possible by the VPP smart breaker technology, we’re creating a more valuable node for the grid while also giving homeowners a clever backup solution.”.

Industry observers note that the integration addresses one of the longstanding challenges of whole-home backup: how to provide broad electrical coverage without having large household loads drain available battery capacity too promptly or cause the nano-grid to immediately fail after an off-grid transition due to excessive inrush current. With the newly expanded VPP smart breaker technology digitally integrated with the sonnen ecosystem, the system can intelligently shed large loads without requiring those circuits to be relocated. ADAPT Energy keeps the smart breakers synchronized with the sonnen battery during backup mode and automatically restores the breakers when grid power returns. This significantly reduces installation complexity and tedious inspections for installers, allowing crews to complete more jobs per week.

Industry observers note that for homeowners, the system provides the convenience of a whole-home electrical configuration that intelligently manages the loads that have the greatest impact on backup duration. This work is all done in the background, meaning homeowners do not have to worry about resetting individual circuits during an outage. Instead, participating homes will see more value from their VPA program in the form of an enhanced backup power experience. Furthermore, at any time in the future, if a homeowner is interested in altering which of their VPP smart breaker-controlled loads are shed during an outage, the process to make such a change is quick and easy, requiring no electrical reconfiguration.

“This is about making whole-home backup work the way homeowners expect it to,” said Troy Morgan, President of PanTech Design, the developer of ADAPT Energy. “Instead of putting the pressure on homeowners to change the way their home is wired and to manually manipulate loads during an outage, we’re putting intelligence into their energy system, which provides a seamless and automatic backup power experience for their home. Our technology empowers home loads to supply optimal backup power during an outage or provide valuable flexibility to the grid.”.

Sources indicate that the permission-based architecture aligns the interests of the homeowner, battery owner and utility. The real opportunity comes when homeowners choose to opt in to allow the breakers to participate in on-grid VPP events.

Sources indicate that when a VPP event is dispatched, the sonnen battery can discharge or charge in concert with direct load shedding via ADAPT. ADAPT Energy will strictly shed pre-approved household loads, and by using Eaton AbleEdge breakers, ADAPT achieves this right where the breaker sits, without relocation. A customer who has opted to include a pool pump, for example, can have that load temporarily turned off while the sonnen battery is discharging to the grid. That way, the VPP can respond through both energy stored in the battery and energy that would have otherwise been consumed by the home, thereby increasing the dispatched injection into the grid, by the VPP.

According to recent reports, “With the addition of ADAPT Energy’s VPP smart-breaker technology to the SOLRITE–sonnen ecosystem, we are expanding the virtual power plant from a battery-centered resource into a fully orchestrated home-energy platform,” stated Blake Richetta, Chairman and CEO of sonnen Inc. “By synchronizing energy that has been harnessed in our battery with intelligent, real-time control of household electrical loads, we can deliver more flexible, responsive capacity to the grid precisely when it is needed most. This integration materially strengthens the value of SOLRITE’s virtual power plant—supporting grid reliability, creating greater customer value, and enabling SOLRITE to continue delivering industry-leading solar-plus-storage VPA solutions to homeowners.”.

Press release from www.sonnenusa.com.

Recent findings suggest that audi has delayed the introduction of the electric A4 sedan by roughly one year, according to Autocar, which quotes an inside source at the German automaker. The electric A4, which was supposed to go into production at the company’s main plant in Ingolstadt in 2028, will go head-to-head with the BMW i3 and Mercedes-Benz C-Class EVs, which are already available in Europe.

The delay is reportedly tied to the Volkswagen Group’s worsening financial situation, software woes linked to the long-delayed Scalable Systems Platform (SSP), and Audi’s desire to make significant changes to the underbody of what should have been a common design across SSP-based electric sedans.

The current-generation Audi A5, which replaced the A4, is available with a plug-in hybrid powertrain.

According to recent reports, autocar’s source stated that the premium German automaker requested bespoke footwells for both front and rear passengers instead of the completely flat floor that many purpose-built EVs use today. The reason behind this big demand reportedly has to do with the brand’s desire to deliver the packaging, seating position, and interior proportions that have traditionally been offered by the A4.

In a recent development, what’s more, the BMW i3 rival will supposedly use a 48-volt electrical system for its accessories instead of the traditional 12V setup that had been planned originally. Just like in the Tesla Cybertruck, adopting a higher-voltage system enables the automaker to use thinner-gauge wire and install higher-powered computers.

However, the changes come at a tough time for Audi’s parent manufacturer, VW Group, which is ditching grandiose looks and doing everything it can to limit the cash bleeding. The upcoming Volkswagen ID. Golf, which is also based on the SSP architecture, has been delayed, leaving the marque with its current lineup of electric models until the end of the decade.

For what it’s worth, the VW Group’s fresh lineup of affordable EVs is doing very well in Europe, but the money problem persists. The company can’t make them fast enough to keep up with demand, but building gas cars is still more profitable. This conundrum has put the German auto industry giant in a tough spot, where it’s trying to keep factories alive, but the importance of the vehicles that are at the moment being assembled there is slowly fading.

The first SSP-based cars were originally planned for 2026, but so far, not a single production model has been assembled.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finding qualified equipment operators is hard enough for most mining companies, and the extreme weather, punishing conditions, and oxygen-deprived air of the Tibetan mountains combine to make finding operators even tougher for the operators if this high-altitude copper mine – but SANY thinks they have a solution: fully self-driving haul trucks.

Chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet. Operated by Zijin Minig and Tibet Julong Copper, the mine functions at a dizzying 17,700 foot elevation in a region of the Gangdese Mountains known as the Kailas Range, and the conditions there would challenge the health and safety of even the toughest and fittest operators.

Sources indicate that “High-altitude illness becomes increasingly relevant above 2,500 meters,” explains Eacon, in one section of a published paper. “Research involving workers in Andes mines operating between 3,800 and 4,500 meters found that 73% of workers assessed experienced periods of nocturnal oxygen saturation below 85% during their high-altitude shifts, indicating moderate-to-severe hypoxemia.”.

That’s bad news for Zijin’s workers – but the good news here, of course, is that the organization won’t be needing many heavy haul drivers going forward.

SANY has been working with Perth, Australia-based Eacon Mining Technology to develop an autonomous haulage solution that uses a full suite of both in-vehicle and ground-based sensors, adaptive vehicle controls, and machine learning that can handle the major bad trucks even here in the Kailas range.

“Autonomous haulage offers one way to address this challenge,” continues the Econ report. “Rather than requiring a driver for each truck, autonomous systems allow fleets to be managed through centralized supervision, with personnel overseeing operations and intervening when required. This reduces the need for people to spend entire shifts operating equipment at elevation, while changing how workforce resources are allocated across the mine … depending on the system configuration, some operations can manage autonomous fleets from remote Integrated Operations Centers located away from the mine site, (allowing) personnel to supervise haulage activities from lower-altitude locations, further reducing the need for workers to remain in extreme-altitude environments.”.

The working partnership between the two companies combines SANY’s battery-powered truck platform with Eacon’s full technology stack to create dependable, driverless haul trucks with logic and behaviors that are ideally suited to China’s open-pit mining environments.

Eacon technology is currently operating more than 3,100 autonomous trucks cross more than 40 large-scale mines, including Zijin Mining’s Zijinshan Gold-Copper Mine and at the Norton Gold Fields project in Australia.

Sources indicate that while specifications for this specific deployment weren’t disclosed, the SANY SKT105E trucks (the “D” is, presumably, the wide-body variant) the company has deployed elsewhere are powered by a dual-motor electric drivetrain, pairing two permanent-magnet synchronous motors with a dual three-speed automated manual transmission. The system delivers 570 kW (~765 hp) of continuous power and up to 820 kW (~1,100 hp) at peak output, with each motor producing some 2,430 Nm (~18,00 lb-ft) of peak torque.

In a recent development, those motors get their electrons from an absolute whopper of a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery pack in capacities ranging from 423 to 642 kWh, depending on configuration. The significant trucks also offer regenerative braking to recover energy on downhill runs, while their fast-charging system can reportedly charge the battery from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Many auto dealerships have a well-earned reputation for making life difficult for customers, but it doesn't always get easier trying to rent.
  • According to the JD Power 2026 North America Rental Car Satisfaction Study, overall customer satisfaction saw some notable improvements over 2025 — especially in two key areas.
  • It has been revealed that as for what goes into the results, JD Power bases them on ease of rental, pick-up/drop-off, level of trust, vehicle, staff, value for price paid, and digital tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Many auto dealerships have a well-earned reputation for making life difficult for customers, but it doesn't always get easier trying to rent. Whether they're charging customers for breaking the laws of physics or relying on AI scanners to bill $440 for a wheel scuff, rental car agencies obviously have some work to do when it comes to boosting customer satisfaction. The good news is that that seems to be happening.

According to the JD Power 2026 North America Rental Car Satisfaction Study, overall customer satisfaction saw some notable improvements over 2025 — especially in two key areas. First, 90% of rental car customers mentioned that, when they arrived at the counter, a vehicle from the class they reserved was waiting for them. That is, they reserved a mid-size sedan and one was there. Getting a bit more detailed, 85% claimed they "were able to pick a specific vehicle within the class they were given." Those figures were up 3 and 5 percentage points, respectively. Meanwhile, the study's average satisfaction score went from 691 in 2025 — on a 1,000-point scale — to 707 this year.

It has been revealed that as for what goes into the results, JD Power bases them on ease of rental, pick-up/drop-off, level of trust, vehicle, staff, value for price paid, and digital tools. Those seven "core dimensions" are then weighted in the order they're listed. The outcome for 2026 was that six of 13 agencies finished with above-average scores, led by Enterprise, National, Advantage Rent A Car, Alamo, Sixt, and Hertz. Bringing up the rear were Thrifty and Dollar. Finally, all this data comes from 7,845 survey respondents, all of whom had rented their cars from airport-based rental companies in the span between August 2025 and August 2026.

Industry observers note that it's worth pointing out that all 13 rental agencies earned higher study scores this year than last, with a lot of that improvement coming at the lower levels. Dollar, for instance, was at the very bottom of the rankings for both 2025 and 2026, yet its score jumped from 641 to 663. The biggest advance in terms of points was for Payless — it went from 11th place with 650 points last year to 8th place with 699 points this time around.

The standings didn't change much at the other end of the spectrum, though. The order remained the same, with Enterprise setting the pace, followed by National and Advantage Rent A Car, and they each saw essentially the same improvements: Enterprise was up 5 points to 739, National improved the same amount to 726 points, and Advantage advanced 6 points, rising from 711 to 717. (Technically, Advantage was tied with Sixt in 2025. Despite a three-point bump in its satisfaction score, that last agency slipped to fifth place in 2026, falling behind Alamo's 716 points.).

Oh, and there's one other factoid you should keep in mind about the rental car agencies: every major rental car brand in the country is owned by one of three companies.

Enterprise Mobility owns Enterprise, of course, but it has National and Alamo under its umbrella as well. Likewise, Avis Budget Group controls its namesake rental brands plus Payless, and Hertz has its own trio that extends to Dollar and Thrifty. Hertz also had purchased Advantage and owned that brand for a time. It's just that when Hertz bought Dollar and Thrifty in 2012, the FTC forced Hertz to sell off Advantage to maintain a competitive market.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new IEA report finds renewables are already strengthening energy security and competitiveness while cutting fuel import costs—but faster electrification, grid modernization, and greater flexibility can extend these gains across the economy.

It has been revealed that spain’s rapid expansion of renewable power has strengthened its energy security and competitiveness, but faster electrification across transport, buildings, and industry will be essential to meeting the country’s energy and climate goals, according to a new IEA Energy Policy Review published Oct. 5, 2026.

Between 2015 and 2025, renewables’ share of Spain’s electricity generation increased from 35% to 56%, while emissions declined by around one-fifth. These achievements have been underpinned by the country’s strong energy and climate policy framework and its well-established approach to a just transition, which links clean energy investment with jobs, regional development, and social inclusion.

Spain’s growing share of renewable power is already helping to lower wholesale electricity prices and reduce its exposure to imported fuels. Without the vast expansion of renewable capacity, its natural gas imports for power generation would have been nearly 40%, or USD 26 billion, higher in 2024. Nonetheless, imports still provided almost 70% of Spain’s total energy consumption in 2024, underscoring the need to extend the transition beyond electricity supply.

Accelerating electrification of end-uses should also be a priority, the report finds. Today, electricity accounts for just 25% of Spain’s final energy consumption, well below the country’s target of 35% by 2030. Electric vehicle uptake is relatively limited, notably for corporate fleets, while fossil-fuel heating remains widespread, and the industry faces high upfront investment costs.

Sources indicate that A combination of taxes, levies, and network charges are keeping end-user electricity prices high, while fossil fuels face comparatively lower charges in Spain. The country is taking steps to address this, including by abolishing the tax on electricity production in 2026. Further rebalancing domestic energy price dynamics, while protecting vulnerable consumers, could strengthen incentives for households and businesses to electrify and help industry capture the competitive advantages of renewable power.

Sources indicate that spain has debuted reforms to accelerate storage, demand-side flexibility, and adapting grid rules to a rapidly changing generation mix. Continued progress on power system infrastructure and management, alongside a more balanced mix of wind, solar, and hybrid technologies, can help Spain integrate growing shares of renewable generation while strengthening electricity security and resilience.

The review also highlights the importance of carefully managing the planned nuclear phase-out to maintain security of supply. Following the recent approval to extend the lifetime operation of the Almaraz nuclear power plant, the report recommends implementing a transparent framework for future case-by-case decisions that considers the costs and benefits for consumers and the wider power system.

It has been revealed that strong progress on renewable power in Spain demonstrates that its deployment can advance energy security, competitiveness, and social inclusion. The report finds that the next test will be to turn this progress into a fully integrated, flexible, and resilient energy system. By accelerating electrification, modernizing and optimizing grids, unlocking flexibility, and carefully managing its nuclear phase-out, Spain can offer valuable lessons for other countries pursuing similar energy transformations across the wider economy.

According to recent reports, there's no arguing that the people of the city of Detroit tend to keep things interesting. Earlier this year, a priest punched the fear of God into a fleeing teen driver after a crash. The latest stunt to capture the nation's attention was two young Detroit men taking their horses onto a city bus. The outing was Raven's first time in the significant city, according to the Detroit Free Press. Raven is one of 12 horses Jordan Williams uses as part of his Urban City Cowboys program: a Western rodeo school outside of Detroit, as well as an organization that offers equestrian therapy to children with disabilities.

In a recent development, williams was one of the two men involved in the horse-meets-bus adventure. The other was a close friend who had come along with his horse for a fundraiser earlier in the day. While riding near 7 Mile Road, they had stopped near a Detroit Department of Transportation bus stop. One of the buses had also stopped for them and the driver asked if they wanted on. If you listen to the video circulating the internet compiled from the cameras on the DDOT bus, you can hear the driver say to Williams and his friend, "If they can get in here, it is what it is.".

Sources indicate that at one point you hear the amused bus driver mention something about the horses being service animals, and Williams responding with a joking "yup." The driver then lowered a ramp that would allow the horses to more easily walk aboard. Sure enough, both Raven and the other horse entered the bus with the men, trotted down the aisle, and exited from the rear side exit as the automated greeting told the horses, "Welcome aboard." The horses never stayed on the bus, though. They really did a quick walk through.

In a recent development, this wasn't the first time one of Williams' horses has boarded a Detroit-area bus. He told WXYZ 7 that he intended for the stunt to make a splash, as he's had horses "on Jefferson, we've been on the Chalmers, we've been on the Connors and now on the 7 Mile." This was Raven's first bus adventure, though. Raven is a 12-year-old horse, and one of Williams' newest. Along with his 11 other horses, he watches 10 horses for individuals on his 10-acre property in Romulus, along with the typical barnyard set up of chickens, goats, pigs, a cow, barn cats, dogs, a parrot, snake, and others.

DDOT issued a statement to WXYZ November 10 that remarked it is "taking the appropriate steps to address this incident as it is not consistent with DDOT policy and potentially creates an unsafe and uncomfortable ride for our passengers." The rider in the video seemed to be the only person on the bus at the time, and appeared pretty chill about the whole experience while he took some pictures. Also, it could be argued that the horses didn't technically "ride" the bus. It never moved while they were on board.

In a recent development, the city is using the recent attention as a way to train everyone at DDOT to "make sure they're aware of different policies," i.e. service animals. A statement from the city mentioned that they recognized "that the actions in the video were meant to draw awareness to a positive cause. The City of Detroit also stands ready to assist our local entrepreneurs by connecting them with programs and opportunities that safely increase awareness of their organizations, and helps them expand their positive impact on our City.".

According to recent reports, williams' act was truly wholesome, and of course people understand horses don't technically belong on a bus, or in a city environment with all those dangerous cars. Take it from last city to truly hold out on keeping horses around — New York City, which finally voted away its famous horse carriages in October.

#11. Tech Report: Darlington’s First SMR Is Late and Over Budget. Ontario Needs to Rethink the Next Three.

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (893 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cleantechnica

Tech Report: Darlington’s First SMR Is Late and Over Budget. Ontario Needs to Rethink the Next Three.

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (893 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that ontario Power Generation has acknowledged that its first GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 small modular reactor at Darlington will exceed its C$7.7 billion approved budget and miss its October 2030 commercial-operation target.
  • Recent findings suggest that the reason matters.
  • Sources indicate that this is not a story about a construction crew failing to install a basemat.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that ontario Power Generation has acknowledged that its first GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 small modular reactor at Darlington will exceed its C$7.7 billion approved budget and miss its October 2030 commercial-operation target. There is no replacement cost or completion date yet. OPG expects its engineering, cost and schedule review to be substantially complete by mid-2027.

Recent findings suggest that the reason matters. In its November 10 financial results, OPG identified continuing first-of-a-kind reactor engineering and its effects on construction execution and supply-chain performance. Ontario started physical work while parts of the design governing that work were still evolving. The project is now living with the consequence.

Sources indicate that this is not a story about a construction crew failing to install a basemat. The 2.1-million-pound reactor foundation is in place, work on the turbine building has progressed, and the cooling-water tunnel equipment has been assembled. These are real achievements. They do not settle the engineering dependencies, supplier requirements and delivery sequence for a first-of-a-kind reactor. Construction progress and schedule certainty are different things.

Megaproject researcher Bent Flyvbjerg calls the better approach “think slow, act fast.” Engineering, interfaces and execution plans need enough maturity that construction can advance without a succession of disruptive changes. Design and construction can overlap on controlled, ready-to-build work packages. Darlington’s own disclosure indicates that the required boundary has not been maintained.

My TFIE Strategy Briefing on Darlington’s SMR examines the November disclosure, the historical nuclear construction record and the consequences for Ontario’s four-reactor plan.

Ontario is an unusually favourable test for the Western SMR industry. OPG operates a large nuclear fleet and has an experienced workforce, an established site, transmission infrastructure and public financial backing. GE Vernova Hitachi has extensive boiling-water reactor experience. Yet the BWRX-300 is still a newly introduced design, and the promised economies of repeat construction depend on its becoming stable enough to repeat.

The four-reactor programme originally carried a C$20.9 billion budget. Within that were C$6.1 billion for the first reactor, C$1.6 billion of common infrastructure and C$13.2 billion for Units 2 through 4. The financial proposition depends on the later reactors becoming cheaper after the first teaches suppliers and builders how to execute the design.

In my October 2025 assessment I applied historical nuclear construction reference-class uplifts rather than relying only on the project’s internal estimates. A 67% uplift to the Unit 1 reactor component, with shared infrastructure held unchanged, produces a C$11.8 billion first-stage cost. A 202% uplift produces about C$20.0 billion, or nearly 96% of the original budget for all four reactors. These are illustrative stress outcomes from the historical construction class, not upcoming OPG estimates. They show how much of the programme’s financial margin depends on getting the first design and subsequent learning right.

The uncertainty has already reached Ontario’s electricity planning. In its November 10 filing to the Ontario Energy Board, OPG withdrew the Darlington SMR generation forecast from its 2027–2031 rate application. Previously planned production of about 0.5 TWh in 2030 and 1.9 TWh in 2031 is no longer included. The filing does not announce a post-2031 commissioning date. It shows that the earlier production assumptions cannot support the regulatory request.

Ontario does not need to suspend other electricity decisions while it waits for a revised reactor budget. The Independent Electricity System Operator’s May 2026 LT2 energy procurement secured 1,115 MW of fresh wind and solar contracts, with expected annual generation of about 2.37 TWh and a weighted average fixed price of C$88.84/MWh. That is approximately the annual electricity a 300 MW reactor would generate at a 90% capacity factor. Ontario also contracted 640 MW of battery capacity at C$563.48 per MW-business day.

Wind and solar provide energy on a different hourly profile from a nuclear reactor. The battery procurement buys capacity services, not 640 MW of round-the-clock generation. Ontario’s decision is to assemble a reliable portfolio from the newly introduced energy, existing nuclear and hydroelectric generation, storage, interties, transmission and flexible demand. The whole-system cost of that portfolio is the relevant comparator for the next three SMRs, not a claim that a wind farm is a nuclear reactor with a different name.

Sources indicate that this distinction also matters for the C$127/MWh comparison in my longer analysis. That figure allocates the renewable contracts’ initial energy payments and separate battery capacity payments across expected renewable production. It establishes a useful procurement spending benchmark. Additional charging, integration, transmission and dependable capacity requirements must be assessed to establish a comparable delivered system service.

Before Ontario commits to Units 2 through 4, it should require a credible outside-view update of the first unit’s cost and schedule, disclosure of outstanding design packages and their interfaces, measured evidence of construction learning, and a system-level comparison against resources that can be delivered during the same period. Each proposed later reactor is an investment decision, not an automatic entitlement created by spending on the first.

Ontario’s existing nuclear fleet is a valuable low-carbon resource. Keeping it productive and refurbishing it where justified remains vital. The problem is treating a first-of-a-kind nuclear construction programme as reliably cheap future supply before engineering and costs support that conclusion.

Read the full Darlington assessment for the reference-class cost exposure, financing sensitivities and the investment gates Ontario should apply. The linked Flexibility Mesh report develops the system-services and grid-utilisation side of the comparison.

Recent findings suggest that autonomous lawncare specialists Greenzie passed a major milestone with their self-driving mowers last week, surpassing 255,000 cumulative robomowing miles. For context, that’s far enough to mow every inch of space between the Earth and Moon.

Greenzie announced the self-driving milestone last week, and it’s genuinely impressive, reflecting Greenzie Powered Autonomy mowing more than 9 billion (with a b) square feet of turf across more than 200 commercial customers, 45 US states, and more than 500,000 equivalent man-hours of mowing.

And, while I might have pointed the fact that Greenzie mowers have covered more miles in its press release than Daimler’s entire hydrogen truck fleet, the organization really seems to be leaning into the Moon angle.

“We mowed to the moon, but the real achievement is the commercial experience behind those miles,” states Charles Brian Quinn, co-founder and CEO of Greenzie and almost definitely the guy who first came up with the lunar lawncare line. “Every mile represents equipment working on real properties with commercial crews. That experience has shaped our technology, strengthened our OEM partnerships and taught us how to help customers successfully integrate autonomy into their daily operations.”.

Greenzie develops autonomous packages for, and maintains OEM relationships with electric brands Mean Green Electric Mowers (whose Vanquish Autonomous commercial mower is shown, above), and Greenworks Commercial, as well as gas-powered brands like Bobcat and Wright Manufacturing. Regardless of what powers the mowers, Greenzie supplies the self-driving technology and integration expertise, while its OEM partners develop and manufacture the equipment that does the actual cutting, clearing, and whatever else their clients need.

Sources indicate that “Successful autonomy requires more than capable technology,” said Steve Bush, chief operating officer of Greenzie. “Customers need to understand where autonomy fits into their operations, how to prepare their crews and how to measure success. We have spent years learning those lessons alongside our customers and OEM partners, creating a more consistent path to adoption as the industry grows.”.

The Mean Green Vanquish Autonomous featured gere is a fully electric, stand-on, zero-turn (ZTR) mower built around an all-day-ready 22 kWh li-ion battery pack and featuring a 60″ rear-discharge mulching deck.

Mean Green claims that the combination of big battery and the electric motors that drive the ZTR mower and spin up its blades are good up to eight hours of continuous mowing on a charge, with an aluminum chassis and deck helping to keep the machine’s overall weight down for easier towing maximum efficiency.

The firm states the mower can operate in either manual or autonomous mode, with Greenzie’s self-driving software supported by six depth-sensing stereo cameras providing 360-degree vision, RTK-corrected GPS, and visual-inertial odometry for onboard site mapping and precise positioning, which Greenzie says allows the mower to detect obstacles up to twenty feet away, recognize designated keep-out zones, and automatically return to its starting point when called back.

A top speed of 11.5 mph and the ability to repeat saved mowing routes, the Vanquish is designed to give commercial landscaping crews another productive worker without adding another person to the payroll … which, with a $60,000 asking price, is money they will probably still need.

Let’s get some pro-labor rage going in the comments, and don’t forget to mention what kind of paycheck you’d need to get to go work in landscaping 2,000+ hours a year while you’re there.

#8. The Chevy El Camino Introduced In 1959, And This Is The Ute's Most Sought-After Model Year

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (575 w)
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik

The Chevy El Camino Introduced In 1959, And This Is The Ute's Most Sought-After Model Year

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (575 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that no, the Chevy El Camino wasn't the first to combine a two-door car with an open bed truck.
  • Industry observers note that of course, it was the 1957 Ford Ranchero that truly inspired the El Camino.
  • Recent findings suggest that this is where things start to get interesting for gearheads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that no, the Chevy El Camino wasn't the first to combine a two-door car with an open bed truck. The first production vehicle to do that was a Ford, but possibly not the one you're thinking of. A design engineer named Lew Bandt, then with Ford of Australia, developed what's often considered the original factory-made ute — the 1934 Ford Model 40-A Light Delivery. Depending on exactly how you define a ute, some folks point to the 1927 Volvo OV4 as well.

Industry observers note that of course, it was the 1957 Ford Ranchero that truly inspired the El Camino. The Ranchero was built on the Blue Oval's full-size platform of the time, and it became both relatively popular and relatively profitable for the automaker. In fact, it was successful enough that Chevy was inspired to get in on the ute action with its full-size 1959 El Camino. Originally a short-lived model only in production for that year and 1960, the El Camino would get a second chance at life in 1964. That's when the Bowtie brand revived the name and brought it back in slightly downsized form on the same platform as the intermediate-class Chevrolet Chevelle.

Recent findings suggest that this is where things start to get interesting for gearheads. In 1970, Chevrolet introduced a 454-cubic-inch LS6 V8 that was reserved for both the Chevelle and its platform mate. With that mill standing out as the most powerful unit of the year, the former became a muscle-car legend and one of Dom Toretto's rides in the epic 10-movie "Fast and Furious" saga. Meanwhile, the latter turned into perhaps the most sought-after El Camino of them all, the 1970 El Camino SS LS6 454. Keep in mind that this was a whole different engine than the LS6 in the 200-mph 2027 Chevrolet Corvette Stingray.

There are two key reasons that enthusiasts crave this machine. Right off the bat, the 1970 El Camino SS 454 was a one-year wonder — its exact powerplant was the aggressive LS6 V8 that would be dropped from the El Camino for 1971. True, Chevy sold a 1971 El Camino SS 454, but that mill was the less-powerful LS5. As far as actual production numbers for the 1970 model, those are hard to come by. Hemmings says 4,475 Chevrolets in total were sold with the LS6 for that year, but they were spread out among both Chevelles and El Caminos.

It has been revealed that the second major selling point here is the outrageous driving experience offered by these rides, and for that, credit also goes to their incredible engine. Factory rated at 450 horsepower with a whopping 500 pound-feet of torque, this motor featured a cast-iron block and heads along with an 11.25:1 compression ratio. Also adding to the muscle are a four-bolt main block, a four-barrel Holley carburetor, and a high-performance camshaft. The outcome was that both the El Camino and Chevelle could serve up more horses than not just the 1970 Corvette, but all other production cars, too.

As further proof of just how hard people are jonesing for the 1970 El Camino SS LS6 454, an example may hold the record for the highest auction price for any El Camino — the car went for $275,000 at a Barrett-Jackson sale in 2023. Just remember auction values can change promptly: one 1970 Chevelle LS6 lost its owner a million dollars.

#7. Scout Steps Toward Mass Production, With 200,000+ Reservations On The Line

Scout Steps Toward Mass Production, With 200,000+ Reservations On The Line

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scout Motors, the revived American brand now focused on off-road capable and affordable electric trucks and SUVs, has apparently produced its first validation build vehicles at its factory in South Carolina.
  • Industry observers note that we’ve seen many EV startups come and go, including ones that revived old, historic car brands — like Detroit Electric.
  • Recent findings suggest that oh, also, the company has a $2 billion factory in South Carolina, and it’s real.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scout Motors, the revived American brand now focused on off-road capable and affordable electric trucks and SUVs, has apparently produced its first validation build vehicles at its factory in South Carolina. This is a significant step forward toward mass production for the Volkswagen Group subsidiary.

Industry observers note that we’ve seen many EV startups come and go, including ones that revived old, historic car brands — like Detroit Electric. However, in this case, Scout is 1) offering something unique on the market, 2) focused on affordability combined with usefulness, 3) backed by automotive giant Volkswagen Group, and 4) currently has more than 200,000 reservations on the books! Reportedly, there are 212,000+ reservations for Scout EVs.

Recent findings suggest that oh, also, the company has a $2 billion factory in South Carolina, and it’s real. I’m sure there’s a lot to do there to get it filled out and operating as desired, but getting to factory production of validation build vehicles is a notable achievement that implies we are fairly close to getting actual production vehicles delivered to customers. The validation builds are of the Traveler SUV and Terra pickup truck.

The company is now able to do stamping, welding, and painting at the factory in Blythewood, South Carolina, and CEO Scott Keogh claims the factory is actually 85% complete already.

After validation builds, the next phase will be pre-production vehicles. Keogh forecasts that actual production of consumer cars will begin in 2027, and deliveries will then commence in 2028. (So, customer vehicle production must be slated for the end of next year.) Construction on the factory began in 2023.

Sources indicate that scout was initially only going to produce 100% electric vehicles. However, it pivoted to also producing extended-range electric vehicles (vehicles that always run on electricity from a battery but whose battery can be recharged from a gas engine while driving). According to the firm, 87% of those 212,000+ reservations are for the range-extended versions of the Traveler and Terra. Buyers are also heavily favoring the SUV, the Traveler, which has pulled in 75% of the reservations so far.

Keogh thinks the manufacturer could reach 400,000 reservations by the time it starts producing customer vehicles. It was at 160,000 in March and 50,000 in January. The factory is supposed to have an annual production capacity of 200,000. Having reservations for two years worth of production would be a strong, helpful boost for the company.

All of that said, one warning on the reservation tally is it has one of the same complications as the Tesla Cybertruck had — reservations are fully refundable and only cost $100. That makes it very hard to know how many people will actually go ahead and buy the vehicles once they are on offer. We will see.
